summary:
## Project Overview

This project is a detailed diorama of **12 Grimmauld Place**, the hidden Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix from *Harry Potter*. The key feature is the mechanical function where the central building emerges from between two identical neighboring houses, replicating the magical reveal from the story.

## Mechanical System

The diorama's signature movement is powered by an **Arduino** and a **motor**.

*   **Mechanism**: The system converts the motor's **rotational motion** into **linear motion** to slide the building sections apart and together.
*   **Prototyping**: The final working design was the result of extensive experimentation and refinement.

> [!NOTE]
> Achieving a smooth mechanical effect requires significant trial and error. The video shows the final successful version, but it took dozens of variations to perfect.

## Styrofoam Modeling Techniques

The primary construction material for the buildings and ground is **Styrofoam**.

*   **Blueprinting**: Designs are first drawn on paper, then transferred to the Styrofoam using tracing paper and a drilling technique to mark key points.
*   **Brickwork**: Individual brick pieces (**2.5 mm height**) are cut and applied. Crumpled **aluminum foil** is pressed onto the surface to create a realistic brick texture.
*   **Ground**: The sidewalk and roadway are carved from Styrofoam. The sidewalk that moves with the houses is detailed with broad stones, while the hidden floor of the headquarters is carved to look like gravel.

## Painting and Finishing

A multi-step painting process creates a realistic and aged appearance.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Before painting, **gesso** must be applied thoroughly (diluted and in several coats) to seal the Styrofoam and ensure a neat, even finish.

*   **Color Palette**: The main building is painted a **dark gray**, while the neighboring houses are a **bright beige**. The stone pavement is painted in various colors with soil tones in the gaps.
*   **Weathering**: To simulate an old building, weathering effects are applied. Joints between bricks are defined by applying a watery white paint wash.
*   **Light Blocking**: Black gesso is painted on the back of the models to prevent light from bleeding through the thin material.

## Detail and Prop Work

Numerous small details and props bring the scene to life.

*   **Architectural Features**: Balconies, staircases, fences, and window frames (using knitting nets for mesh) add realism.
*   **Windows & Interiors**: Windows are made from coated film paper. Curtains are created from **painted wet tissues**. The rooms behind the windows are given depth with photo cutouts and internal lighting.
*   **Street Props**: The scene is populated with various props, including:
    *   Flowerbeds with soil powder.
    *   A street lamp made from a paper straw.
    *   Drainage pipes, wooden debris, and even "internet lines for the Muggles."
transcription:
## Introduction: The Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix

Hello, this is Nauplea. I injured my finger during the work process. From the middle of the video, my fingernail may appear slightly untidy. Fortunately, it has now fully healed!

This work is the Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix. It's actually called Grimmauld place 12 in the UK. This is actually the headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix hidden.

## Building and Testing the Mechanical Base

I'll start with the base makeup. In the case of mechanical devices, they are made smoothly in the video. In fact, there are a lot of prototypes and trials and errors. In some cases, there were as many as dozens of variations. This is the model that finally worked.

Here is today’s core power source. It's the role of turning a rotational motion into a linear motion. After cutting it to the proper size, it is fitted into the framework.

A circuit is created using Arduino. Arduino and motors are attached to the frame. Shall we check whether it operates correctly? 3x speed. 1x speed. It's working well!

## Modeling the Building Facades with Styrofoam

Now it is time for modeling. After drawing the blueprint, tracing paper is placed over it to mark the key points. I'm going to drill a hole in the tracing paper. Following the holes, dots are marked onto the Styrofoam. Connect the marked dots and cut them. Now, brick pieces of 2.5 mm height will be crafted throughout.

I'm going to decorate the bottom as well. Cut thin Styrofoam. Additional walls are constructed. I'll crumple the foil to express the brick texture. The window frames and the remaining portions are also completed. I'm going to prepare several side walls, too.

## Second Mechanism Test and Ground Construction

Second confirmation. There's no problem. :)

Next, it is time to construct the ground. I'm going to make a roadway and a sidewalk. This is the sidewalk. The sidewalk on the roadway will move. Broad stones are carved into the sidewalk. The secret floor of the headquarters is carved in gravel form. The floor is going to move like this.

## Crafting Architectural Details and Prepping for Paint

Now, for the supplementary structures. Both the window frame and the wire mesh were expressed using a knitting net. Balcony. Staircases. Fence. I'll figure out the location first. A door ornament. The front door. The window frames are prepared according to each size.

For neat coloring, gesso must be applied thoroughly. It will be diluted with water and applied several times.

## Painting and Weathering the Diorama

Shall we proceed with the painting? The overall base color is applied first. I'm going to paint the bottom part with a bright beige color. The color of the headquarters is dark gray. Detailed and shading operations. As it is an old building, it requires weathered effects. Add a lot of water to the white paint and engrave the joint.

The stone pavement of the sidewalk is painted in various colors. Soil colors are applied between the stones. The roadway is simply painted with concrete colors. As this area is the headquarters’ floor, it must contrast with the roadway. Road lines are drawn using masking tape.

To prevent light bleeding, black gesso is applied on the back. The remaining sections are painted as well. Since mistakes in the coloring stage would require restarting the modeling process, it's the most difficult part of my work process. It means that the difficult phase is over now. :) The door is painted as well, completing the process.

## Installing Windows and Adding Curtains

It's almost finished. Doors and windows are attached. Double windows are installed from the front. I'm going to make a window using coated film paper. Wet tissues are painted to create curtains. I put them in different shapes and colors from house to house.

## Attaching Balconies and Exterior Greenery

I'll put on the balcony. Bushes are planned to be attached to the headquarters. It's different from the original, but I thought it would be prettier, so I tried it.

## Creating and Illuminating Interior Rooms

I'm going to decorate the room behind the window. First, I'll make a frame of the room. Photographs of rooms are cut out and affixed to the rear frames. I'm going to make a hole for the light and then connect it. Now we're combining all the parts one by one. Lights are installed in the pre-drilled holes. For the moving fence, holes are drilled and it is attached.

## Building Props and Final Assembly

I'm going to make various props. Flowerbed. Soil powder is sprinkled and fixed with glue. Flowerpots. I'm going to make a street lamp using a paper straw. Wooden debris and drainage pipes. These will each be given as gifts to Muggles. :) Internet lines for the Muggles will also be connected.

Holes are drilled into the ground to connect the lighting. Finally, the border is attached, and by affixing the switch and the title, the diorama is completed.

## Final Diorama Reveal

and by affixing the switch and the title, the diorama is completed.
